contexts.text: Out of His mouth goeth a sharp two-edged sword () = the dispersion of falsities by means of the Word and the derivative doctrine by the Lord. AR 108. AR 117. AE 73.

By the sword out of His mouth () is signified the Divine truth of the Word combating against falsities and evils. ( = the dispersion of falsities by means of the derivative doctrine by the Lord. AR 827.)

By the sword, etc. () = by falsities of doctrine, etc. A sword = truth combating against evils and falsities and destroying them; and, in the opposite, falsity combating against goods and truths, and destroying them... AE 131. AE 385.

And the rest were slain with the sword of Him that sat upon the horse, which proceedeth out of His mouth () = that all from the various heresies among the Reformed, who have not lived according to the Lord's precepts in the Word, with which they were acquainted, being judged from the Word, perish... By the sword of Him that sat upon the horse which proceedeth out of His mouth are signified the truths of the Word combating against the falsities of evil.
These things saith He that hath the sharp two-edged sword () = the Lord, who alone combats in temptations.
I will fight against them with the sword of My mouth () = that (such) will be dispersed.
